findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, so the feature flag check is dead logic
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false on both branches of `if enabled`. The result is that SQL expressions are unconditionally rejected regardless of the flag. The function reads as if it honours the flag but it does not, so anyone who later re-enables the feature will be confused, and the flag check is misleading. If the intent is a hard disable, the function and the flag lookup should be removed and the SQL case should return the error directly. If the intent is to gate on the flag, the negation and the second `return false` are wrong.

findings.title: Stub DB silently replaces the SQL engine and its errors are not tied to the gate
findings.body: DB, TablesList, RunCommands and QueryFramesInto are now stubs returning 'not implemented'. TablesList in parser.go and SQLCommand.Execute depend on these. The gate lives only in reader.go's ReadQuery. Other entry points such as UnmarshalSQLCommand and NewSQLCommand reach sql.TablesList without the gate, so they fail with an opaque 'error serializing sql' or 'not implemented' rather than the explicit disabled message. The stub also has an unused receiver and parameter names in TablesList. Consider making the disable explicit at NewSQLCommand/Execute too, so every path reports the same reason.

findings.title: Module checksums moved between go.sum and go.work.sum without a clear reason
findings.body: The diff removes checksum lines for apache/thrift, klauspost/asmfmt, JohnCGriffin/overflow and others from go.sum and adds them to go.work.sum. Those modules are removed from go.mod as indirect dependencies, so the moves are inconsistent with the stated change. Running `go mod tidy` and `go work sync` should be verified so the checksum files match the module graph and the build is reproducible.
